radiology_report:
Study: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Facility: Jeroen Bosch Ziekenhuis ('s-Hertogenbosch) | Date: 28 Dec 2024
Clinical Indication: Evaluation of a 65-year-old male with a PSA value of 4.8 ng/mL and a prior PI-RADS 4 on screening.
FINDINGS: The prostate gland measures 56.0 mL in volume. T2-weighted sequences reveal a focal area of marked hypointensity within the right peripheral zone at the mid-gland level, spanning approximately 12 x 9 x 8 mm. Restricted diffusion is noted on DWI with corresponding low signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early, focal enhancement relative to the surrounding parenchyma. The seminal vesicles appear unremarkable. No extracapsular extension or suspicious lymphadenopathy is identified.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right peripheral zone mid-gland, consistent with a high probability of clinically significant prostate cancer. Prostate volume 56.0 yields a PSA density of 0.086 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.7257912.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: A routine assessment highlighted a progressive increase in prostate-specific antigen levels. The most recent draw, conducted in March 2024, recorded a value of 3.6 ng/mL, continuing a slow upward trajectory observed over prior years. Given this pattern alongside his age, a urology consultation and multiparametric MRI were coordinated. Urinary function remains completely unaffected, and he continues his weekly music rehearsals without interruption.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial screening identified a prostate-specific antigen concentration of 3.3 ng/mL, marking a slight elevation for his demographic. Lower urinary tract symptoms and systemic complaints were absent. A subsequent test was planned for later in the calendar year to track progression. He maintained his existing lifestyle and exercise regimen, with no urgent clinical actions required at that time.
